Average Dropout Incidence over Accrued Subjects

Source: R/f_design_plan_survival.R
dot-getDropoutProportionsGroupwise.Rd

Calculates group-specific expected dropout proportions among subjects enrolled by a calendar-time horizon, using piecewise constant accrual.

Usage

.getDropoutProportionsGroupwise(
  time,
  accrualTimeVector,
  accrualIntensity,
  lambda1,
  lambda2,
  piecewiseSurvivalTime,
  phi,
  allocationRatioPlanned = 1
)

Arguments

time

Single finite calendar time since recruitment began.

accrualTimeVector

Accrual interval boundaries; a leading zero is inserted if absent.

accrualIntensity

Accrual rates, recycled across accrual intervals.

lambda1, lambda2

Normalized event hazards for the two groups.

piecewiseSurvivalTime

Normalized event-hazard interval start times. Ignored for a group with a single event hazard.

phi

Vector of exponential dropout hazards for the two groups.

allocationRatioPlanned

Constant planned treatment-to-control ratio.

Value

A numeric vector of length two. Unavailable horizons, empty accrued denominators, and groups without allocation yield missing proportions.

Details

Averages competing-risk dropout incidence over entry times, dividing by accrued enrollment rather than total planned enrollment. Constant allocation cancels within each group. Follow-up intervals are split at event-hazard changes and integrated analytically. On an interval from v to w, let h be the total hazard and J(v) the joint survival at its start. With z = h * (w - v), the mean incidence is F_D(v) + phi * J(v) / h * B(z). The factor B(z) equals G_1(z) - G_2(z) / z, where G_k is the gamma CDF with shape k and rate one. The second term is evaluated using its log probability to avoid underflow before division. The factor is zero at z = 0 by continuity. This implements the validation specification's expected dropout proportion and analytic dropout accrual integral formulas without numerical quadrature. The survival dropout integration appendix derives these formulas and maps their mathematical quantities to the implementation variables.
